utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom. My apologies for the delayed start. I was involved in another meeting and couldn't be here in time. The witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Welcome back to the courtroom. I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies. Mr. Tolimir is continuing his cross-examination. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. May peace reign in this house, and I wish that today's court proceedings end as God wills and not as I do. I would like to wish a good afternoon to Mr. Janc, and we will continue where we left off yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We saw a photograph yesterday of Tolimir in a civilian suit and civilian clothing. Can you please tell us if that was broadcast, published, a year after the Zepa events, and are there any electronic records of that on a tape or anything like that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I don't know exactly when it was broadcasted, but my understanding is that it was broadcasted immediately after these Zepa events. So I would say around July 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P2240 so that we can see if there is an electronic record there of when this footage was created.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And have you heard the anchor of Television Sarajevo saying that this happened last year in July? Did you hear that part of the translation or did you see the quote? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, that's correct, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you hear it in the Serbian language or in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that in B/C/S language, so it was said like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have finished with this segment of the footage, since the witness has seen that it was created a year after the events in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: You, as an investigator, did you perhaps find out where the Bosnia and Herzegovina Radio and Television obtained the footage P2240, and was the camera able to film it live on the 24th of July, 1995, at Boksanica, that particular segment showing Tolimir in civilian clothing? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to clarify first your quote that I said that it was created a year after the events of Zepa. I think I didn't say that. But from the video, itself, we can see that this portion -- this segment was broadcasted a year later. I'm still sure that the actual footage was created at the time when this event took place. That was on 24 of July, 1995. When it was first broadcasted, I don't know. This particular footage, yes, it was broadcasted a year later, but I'm sure that some other -- some other segments of this same footage were broadcasted already before. And to answer your second part of the question, no, we have no information, and I think we haven't obtained from the Bosnia and Herzegovina Radio and Television when it was first broadcasted. This information was not on there letter, nor was there information about how they obtained this video included in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the date on which it was broadcast?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this particular footage, I would assume, around July 1996, because it says a year -- one year ago, this and this happened at this point. So this particular footage was broadcasted at that time on BH Television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Are you able to answer whether the Muslim television was able to film the events at the time they took place on the 24th of July, 1995, at Boksanica, at which occasion Tolimir was shown to be wearing civilian clothing? Were they able to come and to record this footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why -- to which Muslim television you're referring to. But if you mean BH Television, at that time I'm certain they were not able to film this event. There must have been some Serbian television involved in it, because we have evidence and we have other footages from Zepa from that point in time which were filmed by SRT, which is Radio/Television of Serbia, and also from the Television of the Republika Srpska at that time. Also, there is one footage from CNN from 25th of July, when that journalist from CNN was allowed to enter this area and interview General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. And in this footage, did you at any time see General Tolimir in the suit that was shown in this footage of Exhibit P2204 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are now talking about the footage we have been just watching a few minutes ago, yes, we can see you there in a suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see me in any other segment, other than that one? Did you see me on any other footage? Did you see Tolimir in civilian clothing in any other recordings, other than what we have seen in P2204 [as interpreted]? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only other one would be, I think, the one when you participated in Dayton Agreement. On that, I think, that video, we can see you in a suit. But apart from those two, I don't have any recollection that you are wearing suits. You're always in uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One clarification for the record. Mr. Tolimir, are you referring to P2204 or P2240? I see Mr. Gajic on his feet. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, good afternoon to all. It's a mistake in the transcript. We were thinking of P2240.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was not a problem of the transcript. We heard the interpretation. Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, was this footage, P2240 that we just looked at, submitted to any kind of expertise or any kind of check as to whether it's authentic material or whether the material is not authentic, whether it was perhaps edited and the image of Tolimir in the civilian suit was inserted into the material? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the answer would be, no, we haven't asked any expert for this expertise to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please state for the transcript whether you personally checked the authenticity of this footage, P2240?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say yes, because authenticity can be checked through different means, and there are different ways to check it. One of those would be asking the witnesses who participated in this event if this is real footage of what was going on, and I think we have about -- the confirmation from Mr. Hamdija Torlak, who participated at this meeting, that this footage is authentic. The other way would be, you know, what you can see on video, on what you can hear there. And so we can see Mladic signing a piece of paper, and we were able to locate that agreement from 24th of July, 1995, agreement on disarmament of able-bodied men from Zepa, and this is actually the paper which was signed there. So there are different ways of authentication, and this is what we have done in respect to this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should switch off your microphone if you have an internal discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, was Mr. Torlak asked, during his testimony, whether Tolimir is shown in the image and whether this footage was authentic? I think you testified yesterday that no one was asked that question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was asked for both things. Actually, he was explaining the meeting on 24 of July, and then he was presented this video, and he confirmed that this is, indeed, the video or the meeting which took place on the 24 of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, there is no incrimination here. All I'm asking you to do is to tell us the truth as to what happened so we don't have to speculate. I'm going to ask now to show an insert of the footage on Avdo Palic, and that is the number --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask the accused to repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the testimony of Mr. Torlak is in our transcript of our hearing. The witness was not present, but you were present, and the Chamber, and representatives of the OTP. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good afternoon to you. In addition to the objection that I would raise to the manner in when he put the question to Mr. Janc, saying something about whether or not it's incriminating or for Mr. Janc to tell the truth, I would object to that because I think Mr. Janc's reputation is clear in front of this Tribunal as having told the truth with respect to everything he's testified about. But I would add and reiterate my objection to the extent that I believe that General Tolimir is obligated, under Rule 90(H)(2), to the extent that he is insinuating or asserting that the footage in question is -- has been doctored or has been manipulated in some sense, if that's his position, to put that to the witness, to make that claim. To the extent that he has a good-faith basis to do it, it's appropriate for him to do that, but he is obligated to do that to the extent that he asserts, he contradicts the position of this witness under our Rules of Procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you were asked by the Prosecutor to put your position to the witness before you put -- ask such a question. What is your position?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I also thank the Prosecutor. I'm saying -- what I meant to say is that it wasn't incriminating, as far as I was concerned. It can be incriminating only in relation to somebody who's shown in the footage. It does not refer to the witness at all, so the objection is not grounded. I did not mean to imply any kind of incrimination of Mr. Janc. I just did mention to the witness to speak the truth, and this is also something that you asked the witness to do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At this point in time, just to clarify the legal background, I would like to read into the record the Rule Mr. Vanderpuye has mentioned. This is Rule 90(H)(2). I quote: "In the cross-examination of a witness who is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party, counsel," and in that case you are counsel, Mr. Tolimir, "shall put to that witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears which is in contradiction to the evidence given by the witness." Taking that into account, the Prosecutor asked you to tell the witness first if you are saying that this video is fabricated and your appearance in the video was inserted. You may consult your legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. There is no need. The Defence believes that the footage is not authentic, that the footage in which Tolimir appears in civilian clothing at the meeting with representatives of Zepa. I would just kindly ask for answers to my questions, and I have now stated the position of the Defence. May I now continue with my questions, because I have a lot of other questions that are more important than this irrelevant question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If this is an irrelevant question, you shouldn't put it to the witness, Mr. Tolimir. That would be a waste of court time. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There are actually two aspects to this issue. One is if it's the Defence position that General Tolimir is not wearing the blue suit, as we can see in the video, and the second is whether General Tolimir is asserting that he's not present in the video, blue suit or not, which goes both to the issue of alibi as well as to the issues raised under Rule 90(H)(2). It would be helpful to know what the Defence position is in respect of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir. Mr. Tolimir is counsel to explain the position. I think this is not a question you should address the Court, Mr. Gajic, at least not without an application of your client.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. When I said that earlier, what I meant was the question that was being put to me by the Prosecutor, because that was not relevant. What we're talking about here is only the authenticity of the footage, and not the topic of the role of Tolimir at the meeting or the role he had at a meeting with representatives of the Muslims. All I'm speaking about at this point is the authenticity of the footage, not about the authenticity of the events or the participants and so on and so forth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we are all talking about the authenticity of this footage, if it was fabricated or if it is recording a real scene which happened. The Prosecutor asked you if it is your position that this was fabricated and your appearance was inserted. That was the question of the Prosecutor. I don't think, in light of the Rules, that this is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm not sure I understand what is it that you're insisting on, but I clearly said the footage of myself in civilian clothes is not authentic. I don't want to discuss the issue of editing or not editing. I'm just saying it's not an authentic film. Allow me please to put the question, and the Chamber will have an opportunity to reach its decision. We can speak about it for three hours, otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And may I can make it a bit clearer for General Tolimir, and that is: If he's asserting that the film, which shows him in a blue suit, is fabricated, there are two issues that arise from this. Is the nature of the fabrication that he alleges the fact that it's a blue suit that he appears in or is the nature of the fabrication the fact that he appears in the video at all? And the reason why that's important is: one, that it's mandated under the Rules to the extent that it contradicts this witness's testimony, that he put to the witness that that is his position as to one, or the other, or both, or something else altogether; and the second reason why it's important is because, to the extent that he may intend to assert an alibi defence concerning his presence as depicted in the video, that is something that he's also required to disclose to the Prosecution in advance of raising such a defence under our Rules. So it's important for General Tolimir to put to this witness what his position is, either, I'm not there, or, I'm not wearing a blue suit, or, This isn't the 24th of July in Boksanica, whatever his case may be, but it is essential and required under the Rules that he put this to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Please, if it's necessary to waste time on objections, I can understand that, but Tolimir clearly stated that the footage is not authentic, the footage of him being shown at that meeting in civilian clothes. I don't know what is it that the Prosecutor wants from me. I also asked the witness whether he had checked all the films, had he seen it earlier in some footage, because he wasn't there. I must ask him about these things because he was not the participant of the events. He's telling us that Torlak confirmed it. We will go through Torlak's transcript, and we will see whether Torlak said that this was authentic footage or did he only say, This is Tolimir, after he was shown this person. Please allow me to do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think you don't understand the position of the Prosecution because you are not responding to that. I would like to refer you to page 5, lines 18 through 21, of today's transcript. I quote: "Was this footage submitted to any kind of expertise or any kind of check as to whether it's authentic material or whether the material is not authentic, whether it was perhaps edited and the image of Tolimir in the civilian suit was inserted into the material?" That was the question. And in relation to that part, Mr. Vanderpuye raised his concern. Do you want to add something, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think you've got it correct, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, is it your position that your appearance in the video was inserted?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I still don't understand what is it that you insist upon. I asked a question whether Tolimir, in civilian clothes, was inserted into the footage. You're asking me to elaborate my question. Maybe then it would be better for me to go and testify than the witness, who wasn't present or an eye-witness to the events. I thought I clearly asked what is it that I would like to hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should consult your legal adviser. He is assisting you in legal matters. This is a legal matter. We are dealing here with Rule 90 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and it is not just a question of going on with the examination of the witness, but it's a legal matter if you are conducting your cross-examination according to the Rules. You should consult with your legal adviser.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are saying that the footage is not authentic, the footage of myself in a blue suit. We are not entering into any other issues there, whether someone was or was not there, because this witness was not an eye-witness to the event. I just put the question that you read to me a moment ago, had he seen Tolimir in other footage wearing the same clothes, the clothes that we can see in P2440 [as interpreted]. I don't understand what I'm supposed to be doing now; answering the questions put by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you're in a difficult situation because you're not a lawyer. This is understandable. You are representing yourself, but you have a legal adviser. If he doesn't or is not able to assist you in this matter, I would like to put a question to the witness to resolve the situation. Mr. Janc, have you ever checked if those who were in the possession of the video, this specific part of the footage was edited in a way that persons were inserted or deleted from this footage? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can -- I can say that we, as testified, obtained this same footage from three different sources, one in 2000 already, the second one in 2009 or 2010, and the last one just recently. The only source for checking that would be the last one which we obtained from BH Radio/Television, so I'm not sure if on that letter which they provided to us it is specified anything about the authenticity. But other than that, no, we haven't checked the issue of the editing. And as regard to the authenticity, I think I was -- I made myself clear before, how we can assess the authenticity of the video, itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What kind of material did you receive, as the OTP? Was it a CD, a DVD, was it a video-tape, VHC cassette? I'm referring to all the material you have received.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. For the first time which we received in 2000, this is documentary on Avdo Palic story, that one was on VHS tape. The second source was YouTube, so I downloaded it electronically from that source. So the third source, the BiH Television provided it to us on a CD as well, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The so-called documentary on the Avdo Palic story, as you called it, you mentioned it already yesterday, can you tell us about the producer of this documentary, who made that, who broadcasted it, where was it broadcast? What is your knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The author of this documentary is Swiss Television, and the person -- the director of this documentary was Beltrami, Marco, I believe. And we contacted him through e-mail in order to clarify this specific segment. And as I testified, inside -- within the documentary, when you are watching it, there is this segment going on on a television, and this is commented by Dr. Mehmed Heljic during the documentary. So this segment of Tolimir being in a blue suit is going on on a television, and the camera is filming this portion of video. And what I asked Mr. Beltrami, or my colleague asked him, was if he is in possession of the VHS tape which is going on -- which is rolling on on a television, and his answer was, no, he's not in a possession of this video-tape, and his recollection was that at the time when they were filming this portion of the documentary together with Mr. Mehmed Heljic, that he was in possession of this VHS tape. I contacted Mr. Heljic, I think, two years ago or a year ago in order to ask him this question, if he is in possession of this VHS tape, and his answer was no, and also he was having no recollection, either, who was the originator of the tape at the time when the documentary was made. So I've got no independent information, nor from the director of the documentary, nor from Mr. Mehmed Heljic, where this tape which was broadcasted on the TV might have been at the time, so we didn't get that tape. And what we have used for these proceedings here was then just the segment which we can see on the documentary, itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you, or somebody on your behalf, check this video-tape physically if there were any manipulations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was having this tape of -- on documentary on Avdo Palic in my hand. It's not a normal VHS tape. It's a smaller format of this tape. But we haven't -- we haven't sent this tape to any experts, because according to the director of the film, that's the documentary which they have made. And it was at that time publicly available, so I'm not sure where exactly it was broadcasted, but it was publicly available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that clarification. Mr. Tolimir, continue your questioning, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Janc. Could we please now see a sequence from the film about Avdo Palic, 65 ter 365.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you please tell us whether the footage of Tolimir in a blue suit was something taken from the show on Avdo Palic? And I'm talking about the segment that was recorded in the house of the former war president of Zepa, the footage that we just saw on our screens. And could you also tell us whether this was included into the compilation P740?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the footage I was talking a few minutes ago on the questions by -- on the question by Judge, so this is actually the documentary on Avdo Palic, and the segment, when we can see that Dr. Mehmed Heljic is watching television and is commenting on this video. Next to a TV, you can see that the light is blinking, and I assume that this is VHS recorder. And, yes, we have taken exactly this segment to put it into our trial compilation video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the number, 65 ter 365, is wrong. It is not this document, this film we have seen on the screen just now. Please give us the right number. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a 65 ter 3465.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for this correction. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Janc. Could we please now see P2239 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you tendering the last video we have seen on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 3465 shall be assigned Exhibit D267. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the video was received by the Chamber, but the Registry needs a CD of it. It's not in the possession of it yet, and, therefore, at the moment it's only marked for identification, until you will give a CD of it. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we will submit it either today or, at the latest, tomorrow, and then this issue will be settled. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, would you please look at the document on the screen. This is a document by their Ministry of the Foreign Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina, sent on the 11th of March this year. And then we see, under "Subject," your reference, "03/1-05-4-26/11 of 2 February 2011." So this is a response to a request put by the OTP. And it is stated here clearly, and I will read: "Referring to your paper as noted above, and the request for all video footage relating to Zepa in July 1995, please note that the State Investigative and Protection Agency sent relevant papers to ..." And then we have a number of shortened names of various institutions: "... and TV Sarajevo with the request for their archives to be searched for the requested video footage, and for such video footage to be provided if possible." And then they submitted the materials. And this is my question: Did the OTP ask this from the TV of Bosnia and Herzegovina after Mr. Torlak testified or not? And Mr. Torlak testified on the 25th of August until the 6th of September, 2010.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So my answer would be, yes, it's self-evident that this was after he testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that mean that the OTP had in its possession the footage of a person in a blue suit even before Bosnia and Herzegovina submitted the video materials referred to in the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP had in its possession the video of Avdo Palic's story, the documentary, which it obtained in 2000, and also the two segments from YouTube before Hamdija Torlak testified here in The Hague in this Tribunal -- in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please explain what YouTube is, and who can put footage on YouTube?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. YouTube is publicly-available source on internet where everybody can put their videos on it, so everybody can put their videos on this source, and also then download it -- download them from this source.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The footage taken from YouTube, can they be described as proof of authenticity of an event or could they be anything else?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say they can be anything. But in this case, I downloaded them just to corroborate the other video from 2000 and to compare those two if they are -- they are the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I have to interrupt you again. I'm sorry about that. But in relation to the video from the Avdo Palic documentary, there are more administrative problems. First, there was no transcript up-loaded into e-court. That should be done by the Defence and forwarded to the Registry. And the surrogate sheet the Registry received has the wrong number. It indicates that it should relate to an Exhibit P3465, but this is the 65 ter number. This is a mixture of two different numbers. We need a clear record of that. Please help the Registry to have a record of all documents and videos in an appropriate way. It must remain MFI'd until this problem is solved. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since we identified the segment of the video footage only last night, we will do it today, and I believe by Monday everything will be cleared up. And the 65 ter number is an OTP 65 ter number, so maybe there was just a typo in their document. I assume that is the cause of it, and nothing else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure if this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It seems to be a typo, indeed, made by the Prosecution. Thank you very much. I hope that will be resolved just in order to have a clear record which document we are referring to when we are dealing with it. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Janc. I apologise to you again. The Prosecutor believed that I'm questioning your credibility, but I was really discussing only the authenticity of the footage, and I also believe that this is not very important either for the case or for myself. And I would like to continue now, or we can do it after the break and to discuss your report. Could we please have P170. It's a report drafted by Mr. Janc of the 21st of April, 2010. Thank you. It's entitled "Summary of Forensic Evidence, Exhumation of Mass Graves, April 2010." Mr. President, I just wanted to ask whether the Prosecution want to conduct its re-examination now, but then you told me that it's not time for a break now before we move to a different topic. But still maybe the Prosecutor would like to state its position on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you want to move to the other part of your cross-examination? Is that your intention? Thank you very much. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have understood General Tolimir's position. We have no redirect examination concerning the video material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that both parties agree that this concludes the testimony of Mr. Janc in relation to the authenticity of video footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And this is also the position of the Defence, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We have nearly half an hour left before the first break. You should continue with your cross-examination in relation to exhumations. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We can see on the screen the front page of this report. It's Exhibit P170. Can we please see the contents so that the witness could use it to refresh his recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is my question: You used the term "victims," referring both to those people who were buried in mass graves and to those whose remains were found on the surface. In relation to this, could you please describe what did you refer to when you used the term "victims"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will repeat what I think I already described in relation to my testimony on this issue. The victim was the person who was killed or died in other circumstances after the fall of Srebrenica and Zepa enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Does your report -- or is your report neutral in the sense of description whether a person was killed in combat or was killed in an unlawful way?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My report, itself, presents the numbers of the individuals so far identified from the graves which are mass graves, then individual graves, and also those who were found on a surface, and both categories of these victims are included in my report. I testified, and I was clear, I think, during my testimony so far, that we can find the combat casualties within the category of surface remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc, but I think you didn't answer my question. Is your position neutral; namely, that these people could either be victims or casualties of combat? How can we reconcile this? And did you devote specific attention to this issue in your report so that one can see it clearly? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to respond, but it's not easy, of course, and that's why it wasn't easy to say in my report, yes, that many victims was killed in combat and that many victims are victims of a crime, and that's why I'm making distinction between those who are found in those mass graves and those found on a surface. And I think I was quite neutral in -- when deciding about this issue. Although we have in total, I think, around 700 victims found on a surface, and we can clearly conclude that most of them were victims of combat, we will never know the exact number how many of them were, indeed, victims of the combat, how many of the crimes, and how many of some other acts like suicides or other different causes of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. During the examination-in-chief, you presented the position that all the persons who were buried in mass graves were victims of unlawful actions. On page 2027 of the transcript, line 21, to page 2028, line 2, in response to: "Q. What's the number of people who were killed in combat and what's the number of people who died as a result of unlawful activities?" You said: "I'd say most of them were killed as a result of unlawful activities. They were executed by shooting, and those who were found in mass graves are part of that category. Those who were found on surface, for the majority of them we were not able to determine what really happened to those people. We will consider them casualties that fell in combat." And this is my question: Do you only consider the 688 persons that you found in surface graves as casualties of combat or do you also consider that there are people in mass graves who were also victims or casualties caused by combat?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that most of the people, if not all of them -- or, rather, the victims found in mass graves were victims of the crime; they were executed. And not all of those which were found on the surface were casualties of combat, either. We know that some of them were executed, killed, and left on a surface, and that's where they were found. Some of them committed suicides and were not killed in combat, so we can't say that all of these 688 persons which are found on a surface were all killed in combat. The number would be lower for those killed in combat, based on what we have -- what we know now, based on how many identified individuals we have right now. Of course, this number will raise for a few more victims in the future, but proportionally speaking, it will be the same. Most of them we can consider they're combat, although we'll never know how many, exactly, were killed in combat. But I'm talking about those found on surface. But when we are speaking about those found in mass graves, so we have a lot of evidence talking and proving that they were executed, killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. As an investigator, did you separate the evidence concerning those who were killed or executed and those who were killed in combat so that the trier of fact would be able to take a position on the basis of your report instead of seeing it as a neutral category, namely, somebody can be victim of combat or victim of execution? Did you do that on purpose, maybe?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing was on purpose, but in order to stay neutral on this thing. And when I'm saying that it's not possible, it wasn't possible, and that most probably it won't be possible never to say exactly how many of those found on a surface were killed in combat. I couldn't put the exact number in my report, and then I just put the section of surface remains. I am clarifying it right now, and I clarified during my examination-in-chief and with cross-examination, what those people found on a surface represent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Please tell us whether you can tell us about three or five persons -- at least can you tell us whether you actually have witnesses who would testify to how these people had gotten killed, or did you just mix all that up in your report without being able to clearly show which ones died in combat and which were executed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have many statements of those people, and not only statements. Some of those individuals also testified here in this trial in relation to how they survived certain executions and how their colleagues were killed. And when they named these individuals, I was able to identify them. Actually, not me, personally, but the ICMP identified them, and I was able to locate them in their report, and I put their names into my -- into my report. So there are statements which were reviewed by me, and not only statements, also other documents, evidence, have been taken into consideration in order to conclude certain -- certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Now we're going to look at some of your documents, some evidence. In your statement, you say that a total of 688 persons' surface remains were identified. Can we please look at page 60 in the B/C/S version and page 43 in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Of the document P170, I take it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please now look at that? In the report, it's not clear that you separated or distinguished between the victims of combat and other types of victims. Can we now look at D168, please. This is the testimony of Mr. Butler in the Popovic case. He was a Prosecution expert witness. In response to a question: "Do you know that there are witnesses who say that there were, in fact, 1.000 to 2.000 people from the column who died as a result of these combat engagements? Are you aware of that?"

utterances.speaker: MR. BUTLER REPLIED
utterances.text: "As a gross period from 12 to 18 July? "Q. Correct. "A. I'm not. I'm not aware of the specific number, but that particular number sounds reasonable, given the context of the combat that I'm aware of." And if you see that that Prosecution expert witness agreed that there were people who died in combat, and that he considers that number to be a reasonable number, isn't that number greater than 688 that you cited in your report as the total number of remains of persons found?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown this exact portion of Mr. Butler's testimony during cross-examination when I testified in Popovic case, and my answer now will be the same as it was in that case: that according to my analysis and my report, where we can see that so far 688 individuals is identified, which were found on a surface, that we can say that the total number, because we know that this is not the last number yet, the number will grow, and in total, when sometime in the future the whole exhumation and the identification process will be finished in Bosnia, will be closer to 1.000, not to 2.000. So I will say that more -- that my numbers here included in my report are more correct than just estimate which was given by Mr. Butler, because in my report you have actual names and we can count these individuals by names. We can see in Butler's report is just a rough estimate. So my response would be that the total number, it will be final, it will be closer to 1.000, not 2.000 individuals.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You need your microphone, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. I apologise. That number, was it calculated only on the basis of the documents that you wanted to take into account or was it done on the basis of all existing information at the disposal of the Prosecutor about the number of the victims and the manner and place of their execution? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've tried to take into consideration as many information, as many documents, as many evidence I was able to find, read, and I was trying to put everything together in order to come to this conclusion. And so far, I will repeat, on the surface there have been found around -- I will consult my report on page 6014, the ERN number is ending with this number. We have, in total, 961 surface remains cases collected from the ground until January 2010. So nowadays, we have a few more, so I would say around a thousand. And out of these 961 cases, 688 individuals have been identified so far, and these were a kind of leading information for me to conclude how many of them have been, indeed, found on surface and to come to a conclusion how many of them might be find [sic] also in the future. I would say not many more, because we don't have that many unidentified cases anymore which were collected from the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, these 688 persons that were identified, did you place them in the graves -- in lists and in your records as victims of executions or did you record them separately in your reports? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were recorded separately. In addition to 688 individuals which were found on the surface, we have - and I will again consult my report, page 5 - we have 5.777 individuals which were identified in graves. Then we have also one category which I put under "Others," where we have 76 individuals. So all those together would be the total number so far identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. And all those 5.777 that were buried in graves, do you consider all of them as having been killed outside of combat? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that I already answered that most of them, if not all of them, were, indeed, killed or executed. Why I'm saying "most, if not at all," I can explain, because here, Glogova is the big issue, because we know that most of them there, again, are the victims from Kravica execution. Apart from that, we also know that some bodies were taken from other locations which were picked up along the road, the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road. I think a victim testified here about this procedure going on. And so those were also brought into the same grave. And for those victims which were, according to this individual, around 15 or 30 of them in total, we can't say if they were killed in combat or were executed. That's why I'm saying most of them, if not all of them, are victims of the execution in these mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you thinking of Protected Witness PW-064 when you say this? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to say because I don't -- I don't know the individual witnesses by these numbers. But I believe you are right, so -- but I would rather check the name of the individual, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you would like to give the real name of that person, we could go into private session, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. There is no need, Mr. President. Perhaps he can just look at the transcript page of the 28th of April, 2011. This is page 13445. And the question and the answer of that witness, page 13445, lines 6 to 12. The question is: "Based on all the information available to you, do you know whether there was a total of 400 to 500 people from Kravica buried there and 50 from Konjevic Polje?" And he replied, this is PW-064, his answer: "I said that in my estimate, between 400 and 500 persons were buried while I was there. If there were 50 there from Konjevic Polje from the school, that would mean that there were between 400 and 450 from Kravica."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is that the witness you are thinking of, and his testimony, and is that what you referred to just now in your answer? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And have you just seen that the witness is not talking about 20, but a higher number of bodies that were brought and buried together with those who died in Kravica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, this witness was not quite sure how many victims, exactly, was picked up on the road, but what he was sure, that there was one truck of victims brought back to Kravica, and they were picked up along the road, also in Konjevic Polje, and brought back to Glogova and buried there. When I was talking about that I'm not certain about how many of those, 30 to 50, if he put it that number, was casualties of combat, I was thinking particularly on those who were picked up along the road. Because I think that also this witness was quite clear that the victims found in Konjevic Polje, they were killed there. So we cannot talk about those being killed in combat, so my concern was just about those who were picked up along the road. So not the whole truck which was -- which brought the victims back to Glogova grave were victims of combat, if any at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think now it's time for our first break. We adjourn, and we'll resume quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please show D166 in e-court. This is the testimony of Jean-Rene Ruez in the Krstic case, dated the 14th of March, 2000, page 595, which says that in the Bare village sector, as we can see in the first line, the Finnish pathologist team found five bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: The number which Mr. Ruez mentions is smaller for 80 than the one you mentioned in your report as the number of those 688, so the number is smaller for 80. My question is this: Did these persons whose mortal remains were found in the Bare village identified by DNA analysis? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll just correct the transcript, because you asked about 600 bodies, and in the transcript we see five bodies. Then we discussed this same issue already before, but if you want, I can clarify once more. The Bare area is the area behind Kravica warehouse. It is part of the area which, in my report, is referred as Pobudje area in surface remains section of my report. And in that area, so far 558 individuals have been identified. The number you referred to as 688 is the total number of surface remains, but as I discussed in my report, I emphasised that I categorised surface remains in three different areas. Actually four, sorry. And in Pobudje area, there is, so far, 558 individuals identified as being found on the surface, and, yes, they were all identified through DNA. And when Mr. Ruez was referring here to 600 bodies, and the Finnish team, actually, I still don't -- I'm still not sure when did he get this number, from which report or from which source. But I was able to review this Finnish report, and inside that report we have a number of 30, so 3-0, bodies which were collected by their team in 1996. In addition to that, they have examined, according to their report, 250 to 300 victims or bodies which were collected by the BiH authorities at that time from this same area. So in total, what they examined at that time, according to their report, would be around 300 victims or bodies. So this would be the correct number which I can find from the documents, from the reports, so I'm not quite sure when Mr. Ruez found the number of 600 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. After this, I'm not sure at all what is in your report and what in Mr. Ruez's report. Can you please tell us, in one sentence, whether these 600 bodies were found, and if not, how many of the bodies examined by the Finnish team were found? Can you please tell us the exact number? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. By Finnish team, 30 bodies have been picked up, collected, from the ground in 1996. In addition, that same year around 250 bodies have been collected by the BH. So we have 300 bodies, or body parts, or whatever, so 300. Throughout the years, so it means from 1996 up until the end of 2009, additional surface remains were collected from this area, and that's why, in my report, the total number is 558 so far identified. So it means the bodies which were collected from this area, from 1996 up until the end of 2009. When the Finnish team was there in 1996, only about 300 bodies were collected at that time. So in addition now we have double number, so because I already emphasised several times that this number is growing over the years. So I hope I made myself much clearer now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, this reviewing of information which Mr. Ruez presented, was it reviewed information which he presented when he said that 600 bodies had been found? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I won't say it's a revision of his number, but I would say that the number we have right now, it's much more accurate because we have the actual names. So when Mr. Ruez testified back in -- I don't see here when it was, but somewhere around 2002, 2003, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In fact, in the year 2000, as Mr. Tolimir indicated at the beginning with this document, the 14th of March, 2000.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Back then, you know, he was not having the exact information for sure how many bodies have been collected from the ground. I assume this was just an estimate. Why? Because the actual DNA identification of these individuals started in November of 2001, and my report includes the individuals which were identified by the DNA, so which was done later, after 2000, when he testified. And I think that he referred here to 600 bodies as an estimate, as a rough number of how many bodies have been collected up until that time, and we know that up until that time, many bodies have been collected from this area. We can perhaps take a look into the spreadsheet which was provided to us by the BiH Commission on Missing Persons, and which is having an ERN number and is listed in my report as 0 -- X0189696, and we'll see the actual table how many bodies have been collected every year, or I would say pieces of bodies. So we can calculate, based on that number, how many bodies have been collected up until 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you please look at what is in front of you now and what Mr. Jean-Rene Ruez stated as a witness. He said at the time that: "This area has been processed in 1996 by a team of experts from Finland who were operating in that area in 1996, totally disconnected from our activities, they were collecting surface remains. But it's important to note that 600 bodies have been collected in that area." So he says precisely that, and he said that this has been processed: "These are bodies of victims killed in combat, in ambushes, in shelling, and possibly also in other circumstances which are impossible to sort out between ..." And then there's a dash, something not clear. "... I mean, for us, at least, between combat and other situations." My question to you is the following: Where were you in 1996, and were you working for the OTP when Jean-Rene Ruez worked as an investigator for this Tribunal and this Prosecutor's Office in the field? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back then in 1996, I was not employed here, but I worked for the police in Republic of Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On the basis of what are you then denying and saying that these are estimates which Mr. Ruez mentioned, and he says that these have been processed? Have you read Mr. Jean-Rene Ruez's reports on these activities and the way how these 600 victims who were found at the time in 1996 were processed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I've been looking rather carefully at the transcript that General Tolimir has put to the witness, but I do not see in the transcript that Mr. Ruez has said that the 600 bodies he refers to were recovered in 1996. He's testifying in 2000, and he says: "It's important to note that 600 bodies have been collected in that area." But it is not clear, from this passage, at least, that these bodies were recovered in 1996 or between 1996 and 2000, which is when he was testifying. So if General Tolimir has some other information to clarify that issue, I think it would be appropriate before he puts the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think you have a reason to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in line 8 in both the English and the Serbian versions, there is a sentence which says: "This area has been processed in 1996 by a team of experts from Finland ..." And in line 12 in both English and Serbian, it says: "But it's important to note that 600 bodies have been collected in that area." So he's talking about the year 1996. I'm asking Mr. Janc where he was in 1996. I don't know why this is inappropriate. He answered that he was not working for the Tribunal at that time. I'm just quoting what Mr. Ruez testified as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the objection of Mr. Vanderpuye was not in relation to the occupation of Mr. Janc in 1996, but the way you put this information from Mr. Ruez' testimony in 2000 to the witness. And now you read out a part of it, but you left out a certain portion. And for a better understanding for that, you should read that. And I quote: "This area has been processed in 1996 by a team of experts from Finland who were operating in that area in 1996, totally disconnected from our activities, they were collecting surface remains. But it's important to note that 600 bodies have been collected in that area." Whatever that means, but I think there's no need to discuss that any further. Put your question in a slightly different way and take into account this specific formulation of Mr. Ruez. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, did I quote to you from beginning to end what is noted here and what Mr. Ruez wrote, and did you have an occasion, as an investigator, to read any notes about what he left to OTP when he left the OTP and concerning this event? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read this portion of his statement carefully several times, also now, and for me it's not clear, like it was emphasised by Mr. Vanderpuye. I'm not certain what he was actually having in mind. We would need to ask Mr. Ruez again if he was referring here to 1996 or to all bodies collected from 1996 up until the moment he testified. And also, yes, I was trying to locate any kind of report, information, internal memo, whatever would be on this 600 bodies from Mr. Ruez, so -- and I couldn't locate any of such official note, memo, or document. What I was able to find, though, was this report from a Finnish team, which I discussed a little bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, does Mr. Ruez limit the 600 bodies to the location of Bare in his testimony? Can this be seen from the first two sentences which I quoted and which Presiding Judge Fluegge also quoted, or does this relate to the entire area, as you say?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that he's referring to the Bare region, so again we would need a closer look into what he meant by "Bare," because I think you can -- it's not easy to find this place on a map. But I was able to locate it somehow, and I think it is behind the Kravica warehouse in this Kamenica area which is part of the Pobudje area, where we have the biggest number of surface remains collected.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Let us have a look at what another OTP investigator had to say about the very same event. This is the transcript of the 22nd of February, 2011, from this case, and the witness was Dean Manning. Let us look at page 10218, lines from 12 to 16. And before that, please tell us whether you know who Dean Manning was and what he used to do, in terms of work, for the OTP. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can repeat once more, because I explained during my testimony before that Dean Manning was investigator within the OTP, and he has been dealing also with the exhumations of the victims related to Srebrenica events. And he, for different trials, drafted -- prepared several reports in relation to these exhumations. And also he testified in several -- on several occasions in different trials, also for this trial. And he left the Tribunal, I think, in 2004. And then in 2006, when I joined the Tribunal, I took over the -- these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it credible, what an investigator who was working directly in the field says? Does it have its measure of reliability and weight? Can you say that, as an investigator, or should more weight be given to what is expressed on the basis of documents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In different circumstances, different facts will be important, so it depends what you are asking. I can't give you a specific answer, because for some facts it's more important what can be obtained/seen on the field. For some other facts, it's more important what we can find later on from the expertise which are done. So it's not an answer, one way or another, to say, This is the right way. So both those segments are really important, so -- but it depends what kind of question you would like to put to someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Thank you, Mr. Janc. I have no time for discussion. Please look at the page 10218, about what Mr. Manning said and how he answered to my question concerning the victims from Bare. This is what he says: "A. I was aware that surface remains were being collected. From my memory, I didn't realise it was the Finns. I was not involved in that process. It was two years before I started. I was generally aware of it, but it was not part of my investigation." On page 10219, lines 19 to 25, and 10 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused please slow down when quoting numbers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: ... Mr. Manning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, it was a problem for the interpreters to catch the numbers. "Page 10219, lines 19 to 25, and --," and then it stopped. Please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So after that came page 10220, lines 1 to 25, and 10221, lines 1 to 10. The question was: "Mr. Manning, do you know where the surface remains were buried, in which grave?" His answer is: "Considering that I was not involved in the process, I can say that the surface remains collected were stored for --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. You gave three references, and you should indicate from which of these three you are reading now. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the first reference which is just being read out is 10219, lines 19 to 25.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Aleksandar. I think that this was visible in the text. It is marked with the yellow colour, line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "The surface remains collected were stored for many years in Tuzla in salt mines, in the tunnels that previously were used as salt mines. I saw many of those body-bags and collections of bodies. They were not reburied in that process. They were examined and eventually returned to the families, those that could be, and then buried in individual graves, I assume. To my knowledge, the bodies collected as surface remains were stored in Tuzla by the Bosnian Commission for Missing Persons." My question is this: Considering that the bodies from the location that Mr. Ruez is talking about, the 600 bodies, were transported to Tuzla, and that they were identified and then handed over to the families, can you tell us whether there is a list of these identified bodies and whether there is information about who the bodies were handed over to, as Mr. Manning says? Thank you. Are you aware of that? Have you seen such documents? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that part of those 600 bodies are included in my report which are found on a surface in Pobudje area, and I'm sure some of those bodies, if not most of them, are the bodies we are talking about right now. In order to get information on this issue, when and how and to whom those bodies were returned back, we would need the documents which is kept by the BiH judicial authorities, so, namely, exhumation records, autopsy records, authentication records. For some of them, we have documentation here in-house for some of the surface remains, but for most of them, we don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. If the bodies, at the time that Mr. Manning was working before your time, were in the salt mine, and he said he saw them there and were buried in a mass grave, rather than individual graves, instead of being returned to the families, were you able to find them later, at later stages, in Pobudje, as you said here and as you mention in your report? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those bodies which were collected from the ground from 1996 onwards, they were transported to Tuzla, to the morgue there. And once identified, they were returned back to the families, and families buried them in different places, I assume most of them in the Potocari Memorial Centre. So they were not reburied or placed into these mass graves, because we know from evidence we collected, from aerial images, that when those mass graves were created, then the secondary graves, they were created, and all these facts. And some of the exhumations of these mass graves were already underway in 1996 by the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you for this answer. Could you tell me this, please: Those bodies from the salt mine, did you include them again in the reports on Bare that were presented to us here? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understand what you actually are asking me. But what is in my report under surface remains section is based on data on surface remains which was provided to us by the BiH Commission on Missing Persons. This data included all the exhumations of surface remains conducted throughout the years, their code-names, when those exhumations took place, where, in which area and which place exactly. And when I compared these data against the ICMP data, the identification list of the victims, I found the individuals which were identified, and I could attribute these individuals to the -- to these surface remains. So it means individuals found on a surface in this Bare area were transported to Tuzla, where they were examined, and then they were later identified through DNA by the ICMP. And when that was done, they were returned back to the families, and families buried those bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you then write down in your report as if they were found in Bare in 1996? You stated this in your answers here. I wrote down what your testimony was here, but I don't want to lose time on that right now. You said that the bodies were searched for from 1996 to 1999 and that this came to a total of 558. Then you said that 13 bodies were identified by the Finnish team, that 250 bodies were found by Bosnian organs, and that from 1996 on, a total of 558 bodies were identified. Does that mean that these 600 bodies were not found and gathered immediately, the bodies that are referred to by Mr. Ruez and by Mr. Manning in their reports? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These 558 bodies which are found -- or which are referred in my report as found in Pobudje area are found in the area which spread from the Bratunac up to Konjevic Polje, this hilly area along this road, and part of this area -- bigger area is also Bare, as I understand it, and most of them were found around there. And how I referred to these bodies is not actually "Bare," but I referred to them, as to location, as they were indicated by the BiH Commission on Missing Persons. If you go into my report, section -- Annex B, section on surface remains, which ends with ERN 6015, you would see Pobudje area in my table, and left you would have the names of the locations where those surface remains were found. So you won't find "Bare" here, because I assume that Bare also covers larger area, which would, in this case, be Kamenica, like Kamenicko Brdo, Krajinovici, where most of these individuals are found.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Janc. Can we now look at Exhibit P170, page 61 in the Serbian and page 44 in English. This is Mr. Janc's report from 2010. Page 61 in the Serbian and page 44 in the English. Thank you. Let's take a look at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the 10th line from the top, you mentioned Pobudje, the Finnish team, and you say: "P.M.," and then you say: "DNA identification, 20 individuals." My question is this: Does that mean that the Finnish team identified only 20 individuals? A little bit earlier, you said 13.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier, I said that from this Finnish team report, it's coming out that 30 bodies were collected. And, yes, so far 20 of those bodies or of those surface remains which were collected have been identified. So it's difficult, I would say, sometimes, especially from surface remains, and when the bones are scattered around the area, to assess exactly how many individuals you would collect. Sometimes it's less, sometimes it's more. In this case, I don't claim that only 20 individuals have been collected, but what we can see here is that only 20 individuals, out of those 30 cases which have been collected, have been identified so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. The bodies from the salt mine that Mr. Ruez referred to, as well as Mr. Manning, that they saw them in body-bags, were they all strewn about, as you say, or did they actually have concrete bodies there which they identified and then handed back to their families so that they could bury them in specific places, plots? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, I don't think I understand your question. If you are referring to the bodies which were collected, as I explained and emphasised several times already, it's difficult with surface remains always. And, yes, these are bones mostly which are collected from the ground. They might be in one piece, representing one individual, but for most of the times, only a few pieces or several pieces of one individual have been collected at one point in time. And later on, and especially now when we have DNA examination conducted by the ICMP, it was only possible to re-assemble one individual into one piece, and it may elapse several years until one individual is identified or assembled together into one piece again. So that's why this process might be very, very long. It might take several years, especially with those surface remains. And in some cases, it might also be that not all the pieces were put together of one individual and were already returned back to the families.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. I would kindly ask you to respond directly to my questions. I was asking about bodies that were in the salt mine. Could they have been strewn about the whole territory and identified in the manner that you described? So can you tell us clearly whether they were or they were not? When they were taken to Tuzla, were they strewn about again? Please respond to this question: Were the bodies from Tuzla again strewn all over the area? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies which were collected from the -- from the ground were taken to this salt mine, and there, therefore, they were assembled together and returned back to the families when they were identified. I think that I answered the question, so if not, please, yeah, you can put me another sub-question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, can you show us where you recorded those bodies that were in the Tuzla salt mine? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is part of my report is, for example, the table which we can see in front of us, and these represent how many individuals have been identified so far from certain place, certain area, or from the surface remains which were found in this area. Also, the underlying data --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please, if you can, can you be specific? Because of the time that I have, can you be specific about the bodies from the Tuzla salt mine, where they are in your report; nothing more than that. Thank you. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I can be concrete, but I need to explain a little bit more, because from my report you won't find this information, because all those bodies which were identified, or surface remains, were transported to this -- to this place, to Tuzla, and from there they were returned back to the families. And more than that, I can't tell you. How many bodies have been collected, or pieces of those bodies, is not part of my report, but -- itself. You can't find it in a table, but in underlying data which I'm referring to in my report. So the page before this one, you will see what kind of information we received from the BiH Commission on Missing Persons, and there you will find how many body parts have been collected from certain areas. And from what Mr. Ruez and Mr. Manning testified, they were taken from the location, from the place where they were collected, to Tuzla. So that's all I can testify about. That's all I know about these places, about this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, did you see the report on the identification of the bodies? Did you see a list of persons whose bodies were handed back to their families or any kind of list or record of the bodies that were referred to by Mr. Ruez and Mr. Manning? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that for most of them, and not only surface remains - I'm also referring here to the victims found in graves - I haven't seen those hand-over documents. What I was referring to and I was able to see were the ICMP data on identifications. For some of them, yes, we received documents from the BiH authorities, and I was able to review them, and especially for those individuals and those mass graves which were exhumed by the ICTY, I was able to review all these documents. But in relation to what you asked me, if I was able to review all the hand-over documents, I mean the hand-over of the bodies back to the relatives, no, I wasn't, because what I am presenting in my report are actually the identified individuals so far, and it is not necessarily that all of them have been already returned back to the families. So no such record exists at all, so we are a kind of in an advanced stage with my report, because what I derived from the ICMP data are those who are already identified, so -- but it doesn't mean that they were already returned back to the families.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Can you please answer briefly, without going into detail, because I really cannot understand it, to tell you sincerely. Can you please speak very succinctly so that I can understand you. Under whose care -- in whose care were the bodies in the Tuzla salt mine? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was under the -- under the authorities of the BiH Federal Commission on Missing Persons, and there was also Podrinje Identification Project going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. And are you able to tell us now whether there is a report in the OTP by the Finnish experts, and have you read that report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is such report, and I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you use any information from that report and put it in your own report about the victims found in the Tuzla salt mine? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly from that report, but from this page we have on the screen right now, indirectly, yes, I put the information regarding the Finnish team activities into my report. So far, 20 individuals identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Are you able to provide the report to the Defence and to the Trial Chamber so that we can also see what the Finnish pathologists said, or is this a secret that the OTP is keeping? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not a secret at all, and I'm sure that this report has been disclosed to Defence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I was just checking to see that, in fact, that is the case. The report was disclosed, and I'll give you a date in just a moment. It's the 7th of March, 2008, it was disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. We are going to check that. We don't have any more time. I would now like to ask e-court to show 1D777, please. This is an official note about an informative talk by the Tuzla SDB Sector. We can see it on our screen.
