Since there is no translation, I'm going to read in the heading: "It says, "The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of Internal Affairs, State Security Service, SDB Sector Tuzla." And then there is some lines of work, numbers. In the title, it says "Official Note on Informative Talk," and then it talks about source, "Enver Avdic, son of Sado and Hamdija Halilovic, born July 7, 1997, in Gladovici, municipality of Srebrenica," where he resided. He's a farmer, completed eight-year elementary school, Muslim citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina. At the time of the interview, he was a refugee accommodated in Donja Dobosnica Polje [phoen]. So can we look at the last paragraph of this report or this note. Can we scroll up a little bit, please. Thank you. And you can see -- I asked for the last paragraph on this first page. We can see it now, thank you. You can see that there is an underlined part where it says "1.000 soldiers." We will be reading that paragraph. I don't see it on the screen right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's on the screen in the middle of the second paragraph. It's indicated now by the cursor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I pressed the wrong button, and that's why I lost it on my screen. But I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "In the course of the interview, Enver told us that during the breakthrough of the 285th and the 282nd Brigade sometime at 1000 hours of that same day, a Chetnik para-formation opened strong artillery fire at the remaining brigades and the civilian population that happened to be in Buljim, where, in his estimate, 1.000 soldiers and civilians were killed." And then it goes on to talk about the shelling and so on and so forth. Could you please tell us if you read this note about this interview and read the fact or the data about 1.000 soldiers and civilians who were killed in this attack at Buljim that the witness is talking about? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I read this particular statement. It's possible I did. But I am sure that I read similar statements where people estimated, and I emphasise here "estimated," how many people might be killed at certain places.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on the statements that you read, did you note down at least one or two persons, if not a thousand, on the basis of what you read? Thank you. Did you identify any of those persons as those found on the surface?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based just on the number, what we see here, you can't say who are the victims, so you would need much more information. And in some statements, you could see, for example, that the individuals were referring to their friends, brothers, fathers, and by names. In that case, I was able to check against the ICMP data if those names appear on the lists, and in many instances I was able to identify such individuals as being found on a surface, some of them even in graves later. But from this number, just based on the number, you can't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please answer my question, and my question is: On the basis of the statement by eye-witnesses in relation to the location where the people were killed or are in surface graves, did you manage to identify or record any of them in the report that you provided for the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this particular statement or any other statement in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. You told us that you read several statements, and I'm asking you whether you managed to record at least one person as a surface remains victim in your report.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure I came across these names and I was able to link them with the surface remains. And, no, those information won't be find [sic] in my report directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Since I don't have much more time, let us move to page 2 in e-court, the first paragraph, lines 1 to 3 of the very same statement. So could you please just turn the page. This is what is written here, I quote: "Further on, the source told us that while they were going through Cerska, he noticed hundreds of dead people on both sides of the road whose bodies were mutilated, and he couldn't recognise as anyone." Can one find anywhere in the report any data about these surface victims that were on both sides of the road heading to Cerska?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this is general information about where those surface remains might be located, it's possible that they are part of my report. But because we know that in Cerska, we have a mass grave, and that people were executed there and later on buried, so it's possible that this individual came across these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, but I'm asking you whether one can find, in your report on surface remains, any record of the hundred mentioned here and the thousand mentioned on the previous page. Can one find that in writing in your report, and if so, can you tell us on which page?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and the problem is that I can't link these individuals which are here just in number to any of the identified individuals which are in my report. That's the basic reason. I can't -- I can't link these 100 killed individuals to any specific grave or surface remains which are in my report. I would need much more information. I would need names, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Let us now look at 1D778. Let's have that document on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, what about the last document, 1D777?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D777 shall be assigned Exhibit D268, marked for identification, pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can now see 1D778. It's an exhibit. In the heading, it says "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of Interior, State Security Service, Sector Tuzla." This is an official note on an interview conducted with Alic, Hasan. Since we have little time, I would like to ask the e-court to show us only the second page of the document, line 8 on this second page in the first paragraph, or, rather, 9 to 4 [as interpreted]. Let me quote: "In the immediate vicinity, there is again a line-up of brigades. In the immediate vicinity of these people lined up, the Chetniks had a tree cut and put across the road, and when the column moved, they started firing, using all available weapons. And the Chetniks then made an incursion into the column with the purpose of breaking it up." The source tells us that about a thousand soldiers and civilians from the column were killed, so this second source confirms the claims by the first source. Did you have the opportunity to read this statement by the second source and to obtain this additional information about the surface victims; yes or no? The name is Alic, Hasan, and he's from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible I did. I cannot recall it from the top of my head. And, again, this number is this individual's estimate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, have you noticed that two persons from different villages, who were at the same location, are talking about the same number of victims and are describing events in the same manner; yes or no? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that we can see from both of those statements that they are referring or they are giving a number of a thousand, but I would like to emphasise that this is estimate, and we would need to be very careful about assessing -- when assessing this -- the reliability of this number, because it's difficult to assess, even for trained individuals, how many people would be gathered somewhere or killed somewhere, especially under circumstances which experienced these individuals, so when they were under stress and everything. I would say, as police officer, and I know my colleagues are trained in estimating, for example, how many people gathered at certain place, that even for them it's very difficult to catch the exact number. So if you are a layperson, I think it's really, really difficult, so I wouldn't put much reliability on the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Janc. I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we please see the first page again. I note that it is not included in your list of exhibits to be used with the witness, at least not in the last version, if the number is 1D778, as I noted it down. What is the date of this document? I don't see any date on the first line. The date is missing. Mr. Janc, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I testified, it's possible I've seen it, so I cannot confirm it for the fact. But it's possible that I reviewed it, but I don't have any better recollection than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we please see the last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We can see from this document that it is 11 of October, 1995, the day when it is taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe that's correct. I believe that the statement is taken on that date, although I don't see when it's actually written down, when the statement is actually written down. But I believe that's correct, in any event.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we can see from this line here [indicates] it says that the statement was taken on 11 of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On page 1, the fifth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I didn't see any signature on this document. Mr. Tolimir, do you have additional information about it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this document was handed over to the OTP by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, their Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and of -- Interior Affairs, and their State Security Service. They do not put in names on such documents; they just give some information about the so-called line of work. This will be explained when their witnesses come here. I don't know whether the Prosecutor's Office has the names of people who were taking the statement, but these persons are duty-bound to work as professionals, and provide truthful reports, and to be ready to testify before a court, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. With this additional information, we have enough information, and it will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter document 1D778 shall be assigned Exhibit D269, marked for identification, pending translation. And just for the clarity of the record, it was 65 ter document 1D778. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we please have Exhibit 1D780 on our screens. Thank you. While we're waiting for it, let me just say for the transcript that this is a document produced by Bosnia and Herzegovina's Agency for Research and Documentation, AID Sector in Tuzla, which is just abbreviation for Agency for Research and Documentation. The document is dated 1st of February, 1996. These are minutes of a statement given by Suljo Halilovic, son of Muharem, born on the 1st of February, 1960, Bajramovic [phoen], municipality of Srebrenica. In the second paragraph we can see the following: "In the vicinity of Kamenica, before one crosses the asphalt roads, Konjevic Polje-Kasaba, nearby Kaldrmica, fire was opened against the column from Pragas, artillery weapons and infantry weapons from all sides. Chetniks were very close to us, and I concluded that we were surrounded. We managed to organise and start resisting, making a narrow passage through their lines. Most of the people managed to get through this passage. According to my estimates, about a thousand people got killed in the Chetnik assault, and there were hundreds of wounded. Since it was already night, I could not see or recognise any one of the people who had been killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And this is my question: Can one see, from this statement made by Suljo Halilovic, that they fought their way out of the encirclement and, according to his words, during the fighting about a thousand people got killed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, again, that's what he stated and what we can see from this statement. But the number is, again, the problem factor here, because we have to be very careful, especially when he added, one sentence later, that it was already dark. So it was a real estimate of something which, according to this, he wasn't that sure about because it was dark and he couldn't see precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Could you please tell us whether you interviewed Suljo Halilovic, and is this your assessment of his assessment or are you presenting this as something that you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me, personally, haven't spoken to this individual. Perhaps there are some other investigators. So regarding the number -- the assessment of the number, I think I made myself clear before that it's not easy to assess for a layperson. It's not easy to determine how clear -- how close, actually, to the real number he was when providing "1.000."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, because we've seen in statements of three persons that a thousand people got killed at that location, wouldn't you say that investigators should have talked to these people, the eye-witnesses, because they may have known some of the victims? There may have been people who were identified, certainly people who set off with them, maybe some of their relatives. We can see that some fathers lost their sons, and the other way around, on that location. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure that some of those people were approached and interviewed by the ICTY investigators as well, but not all of them, and I don't know right now who of those have been interviewed and who of those haven't been.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Tolimir, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender the statement made by this third eye-witness, which includes his estimate of the number of dead people. This document is number 780. And I would like to ask for another document to be put on the screen, the fourth statement, which will confirm the previous ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document on the screen will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D708 [sic] shall be assigned Exhibit D270, marked for identification, pending translation. And just one correction: 65 ter document 1D780. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please have 1D782 on our screens. Thank you. Again, a statement given to the Bosnia and Herzegovina organs, in this case Agency for Research and Documentation, Tuzla AID Sector. The statement was taken from Sado Ramic, son of Adem and Dila Malkic, born on the 5th of March, 1966, in Poznanovici, municipality of Srebrenica. Can we please scroll down, because I need the third paragraph of this statement. In the third paragraph of the statement, which is the paragraph just above the signature, six lines above the signature we can read the following: "The shooting lasted for about 15 minutes, after which all the sounds disappeared. According to my assessment, about a thousand people were killed there. We went back to get the wounded people out of there, but it was very hard even to move around because of the bodies. I could not recognise anyone." And we can see in the previous paragraph that it's stated: "On the following day, on the 12th of July, 1995, on the road between Buljim and Pobudje, several shells hit our column, and about 50 people got killed on that occasion." So this statement is discussing 1.050 people killed. And on the following page, lines 3 to 7, there's mention of another 20 casualties. Can we please scroll down on page 2, please. Further, because there is a part that I would like to quote. Thank you, yes, now we can see the paragraph that is second on the screen at the moment, and I quote: "When we came to Kasaba, when we came to the repeater, we had to wait for the dark before we could cross the tarmac road, and we crossed it in early-evening hours. After crossing the asphalt road, we reached Udrc and then continued towards the following mountains, the first of them being Veljova Glava. There, we found the group of 10 dead bodies, and not far away from that location there was another group of 10 dead bodies, which again were people I did not know."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, did you have an opportunity to read this statement, where 1.070 bodies are discussed and also locations where these bodies were found? Wasn't that something that merited the attention of the investigators; namely, to see where the surface remains caused by fighting were, according to the statement of this witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I most probably did see this statement as well, and this individual is talking about three different places where they came across or they spotted these bodies on the ground. First, for the first number, a thousand, my position would be the same, especially because we can see from the statement from that part that he also said that it was already 9.00 in the evening. So it was coming to a dark, if it wasn't dark already at the time. So it's very difficult to assess how many people is there, unless you count them. For later on, we can see that the numbers are much lower, 50 and 10 and 20 people, so I would say for those, especially when he says around 10 bodies seen around this location, that he was more precise when assessing how many bodies have been there than with the number a thousand. Especially now, when we know that in the area of Pobudje where those thousand he was talking about might be seen on the ground, we have today 550 individuals identified. So when he gave this statement, and we have to emphasise in this case this statement was given half a year later after these events took place, he said that thousand people were there, so this is his estimate. And I would say, based on what we know today, that the number was some -- much higher than the real number of casualties there or dead bodies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, let me show you page 3 of this report, third paragraph on it. It is stated there, I quote: "Sometime in November of 1995, together with Abdurahman and another 13 people, I went to Lopare where we were chopping wood for the Serbian East Bosnian Corps. We stayed in Lopare for 15 days and then we were returned to the camp. We stayed in the camp until the 24th of December, 1995, when 134 of us were exchanged; Sokolac, municipality of Gracanica." Since he arrived there on the 24th of December, it took two months before he was interviewed by the state organs. He couldn't have provided a statement earlier because he was a prisoner until then. The fact that he was exchanged later, is that something that discredits all the information contained in his statement, corroborated by statements made by other three persons, concerning the number of people?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course not. And when I emphasised the date, that it was half a year later, it's just for, perhaps, certain details which might be -- after so many months after the events, might not be clear to the individuals anymore. But for some facts, he might be still clear very well. So I didn't mean that all what he said was wrong, no, I didn't mean that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. We can see that he gave the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we need the second break now. You may continue after the break. We resume quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we please have the statement of Ramic, Sado, entered into evidence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received, but only for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D782 shall be assigned Exhibit D271, marked for identification, pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, we have seen the four statements which mentioned a bigger number of victims found on surface than 1.000. Can it be seen from these statements that those who died in combat were also buried in mass graves, as they are not to be found in other locations which are mentioned nowadays?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From these statements, we can't conclude that, because the number thousand I already said that it shouldn't be a reliable one, based on the possibility of these individuals to assess the correct number of the individuals which were found on -- or bodies of which were on the surface. So -- and we know -- just to respond regarding the mass graves, we know that in these mass graves are victims from the executions, and we have no evidence so far, not a single statement, which would point at the conclusion that the surface remains or the victims which were killed in these woods - I mean combat - would be taken from these areas and buried in mass graves, so they were just left behind on the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Please tell us whether that means that, even now, on the surface, some mortal remains can be found in the locations described in these statements which mention the number of victims which were seen by the eye-witnesses? Are they still there on the spot where they were or were they buried in mass graves? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say most of them were collected from the ground throughout the years. And because we can see that the process is ongoing and every year they collect additional bodies from the surface, I would say they will be find [sic] also in the future; of course, not in such massive numbers as it was during first years after the fall of Srebrenica; I mean, 1996, 1997, 1998. At that time, a lot of these surface remains were found there, but nowadays a few additional bodies are found every year. So this number, the total number, will grow, but it will not grow much over 1.000, if at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Does that mean that the assessments of investigators are more important than the facts as presented by eye-witnesses and the events, when one is to draw conclusions? Is it more important, what you may conclude on the basis of some paper documents, that you doubt four statements? And what is more credible, your opinion or the opinion of eye-witnesses? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not about the opinion. It's about the corroboration of the facts. It is important, what the eye-witness is saying, of course, but sometimes not everything is correct, what they were saying, but not because they would be lying, but just because our memory is such that sometimes we are wrong. And in these cases, it's better to support certain allegations with independent sources, documents, or in this case, what I'm testifying about, with the expert findings regarding how many individuals have been identified so far. So a combination of both is important, and one needs to be very careful when assessing the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Can you please be brief in your answers and provide some context when you're answering a question, because this is just a general description. I'm asking you now whether it was necessary for someone of the investigators to go and interview these four persons and then make arguments on the basis of which such conclusion of yours can be drawn, or is it more important that you should state that as your assessment and your opinion? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe someone approached these witnesses and they were interviewed, but I'm sure that they would never change their statement and their -- the fact about the number. So it would most probably remain the same. What I'm testifying here is about how reliable this number is, how close to the real number of what they have seen this number is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. And is our goal to change the facts and change the number or to accept them as the eye-witnesses present them? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say, but my position is that this number is not -- is not correct, based on what we know now, so I'm sure they haven't seen that many victims on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Can you please tell us whether it is possible that there may be persons buried in mass graves who were not members of the 128th Division and the column which was breaking through from Srebrenica in the direction of Nezuk, but that the records also may include persons who died during the attack from Nezuk, in the direction of Baljkovica, with the aim of opening up a corridor? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those mass graves are the victims who were executed. They were taken prisoner and were kept in schools, and then they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Did you answer my question? Is it possible that the lists of missing persons, or persons who were killed, include fighters of the 2nd Corps of the BiH Army who were carrying out a breakthrough from Nezuk, in the direction of Baljkovica, in order to open up a corridor, as testified by numerous documents, and have you, perhaps, seen the footage which shows the column coming out to Baljkovica? It's a column that was moving from Srebrenica towards Nezuk. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure on a missing persons list there are also individuals who at that time were the members of the BiH Army, because if they were killed in a combat, and some of them were most probably also killed during the execution and then put into a mass grave, of course, those people would appear on a missing list. Those who survived would not appear, would not be reported as missing and would not appear on such list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation, Mr. Janc. Can we now please see Exhibit P170. This is Mr. Janc's report from 2010. Can we please have page 63 in B/C/S and page 45 in the English version. Page 63 in the Serbian and page 45 in the English version. Thank you. Here we can see the column, "Zepa." We still don't see it in the Serbian. Here we can see it. As there is no translation as yet in English, we can see, above the last table, which says "Zepa," we can see in English that you stated that in addition, 15 Zepa-related individuals have been identified so far from surface remains collected in a wider area of Zepa. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether, on any basis, Visegrad can be considered the wider area of Zepa, and do you know how far Visegrad is located from Zepa? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how far, exactly, Visegrad is from Zepa. I know it's south of it, and that's why I put it in the wider area of Zepa. And those individuals were, indeed, missing from Zepa, so those seven individuals which we can see related to Visegrad area, that they were missing from Zepa. And we know that when Zepa fall in July 1995, that people were taking different directions in order to save their lives, and one of those directions was also south, and then that's where these individuals were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Janc, do you know that Visegrad belongs to Herzegovina and that Zepa is part of the Podrinje area, geographically speaking, if not in terms of kilometres? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of this geographical difference, but I agree with you, yes, because it is south.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And were these victims found in Visegrad, whereas you ascribed them to Zepa, on the basis of what; just their place of residence? Yes or no. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were on a missing list, reported missing, as being from Zepa after the fall of Zepa enclave. That's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you have in your documents a report about them, how they died, where they died? Do you have the findings of pathologists or any court bodies about the cause of death of these seven or eight persons that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. For all those 15 individuals, I requested the documentation from the BiH authorities, and I referred to these documents which consist of exhumation records, autopsy records, pathology records and everything. And I think if we can scroll down here in B/C/S language -- B/C/S version of it, you will see the ERN number at the end of it. You can see. Maybe in English we go to the same -- maybe the page before. You have a reference to documents where you can find information about the exhumations and everything, and we received it, as you can see, from BiH State Court and Sarajevo Canton Prosecutor's Office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you are an investigator, so we wouldn't read the ERN numbers which you mentioned here in the footnotes. Can you tell us, where did these persons who were found in Visegrad die, as they were deemed to be the inhabitants and citizens of Zepa? Where and how did they die? Can you tell this to the Trial Chamber? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think from those records we can conclude that they were -- that they were killed, that their death was violent, and they must have died in the vicinity of those places where they were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: If they were killed in the vicinity of Visegrad, where they were found, or close to the place called Stoborani, and so on and so forth, why do you then list them in the wider area of Zepa, why? Because Visegrad does not belong to the wider area of Zepa. Is it just because of the report or because you don't know that Visegrad is a town, whereas Zepa is a village? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Geographically speaking, you are correct, it might be a much better formulation to put it something differently. What I wanted to emphasise here was that they are related to Zepa events, that they are related to the fall of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. If a refugee from Zepa dies in the United States, should he be included among the victims from Zepa? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in that case. But we have information from the missing list that these individuals went missing after the fall of Zepa, and they were found not close to Zepa, but in the area which is relatively close to Zepa. And it's nothing uncommon, because I just explained that people were fleeing over the territory south-west, north. We also have example of victims from Srebrenica, which I testified already before, which were found in Trnovo, which is south of Sarajevo, and we are still considering them as victims which were killed after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Would they be considered such only on the basis of reports and documents or according to the locations where they were killed and the manner in which they were killed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most important for me was, indeed, the list of the missing persons, and from that list we can see that they went missing after the fall of Zepa. From this table, we can see where they were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it most important for the Court that they are from Zepa and that they are listed as missing persons from Zepa, and it's not important where and how they died and who killed them? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think everything is important in this case. That area at that time was under control of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Can you tell us whether you investigated the grave in Vragolovi and its origins? How did it come into existence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did review documents that we have on this grave, and also requested some additional documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As it is obvious from the evidence which have been presented today to the Trial Chamber, and also through other witnesses and cases, did these persons die under varying circumstances and in different periods of time, and is the grave in Vragolovi a primary or a secondary one? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When reviewing documentation and also asking the individuals who were present at this spot during the exhumation, it wasn't clear to me if it is primary or secondary. Based on the Eva Klonowski's statement, it's most probably a primary grave, but she shouldn't be -- she wasn't -- during the interview, she wasn't very clear on that point. Based on how the bodies were found, so they were complete bodies, it is most probably that this is primary grave. Still, the possibility that some bodies were moved from somewhere else or placed later on into this grave cannot be excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were the bodies -- was the cause of death stated for these individuals by the teams working on this or by any state agencies of Bosnia and Herzegovina working on this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have autopsy records on all of these nine bodies, and the death for all of them was violent. I think for most of them, directly, shot-gun wounds in the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Did you place them in a mass grave on the basis of how they were killed, or how they died, or did you classify them just by the very fact that they were found together in a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were found in one grave together, and these are the victims of a crime -- of execution, and I placed those victims into my report of April 2010 for my first time because so far we have almost all of them identified already. There were nine bodies inside; so far, we have eight identifications done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Mrs. Palic, for example, testified here, and she said that Mr. Palic had been buried in Visoko, where she lived, that she passed by his grave without knowing that, and that only later the commission transferred the body to the Vragolovi mass grave? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This must have been misinterpretation or misunderstanding, what Ms. Palic has testified about. The body of Avdo Palic was exhumed along with other eight individuals in 2001 from this Vragolovi grave. At that time, they didn't know who these individuals are, and that's why they transported them to Visoko and reburied all of them -- all of them at that place, at the cemetery there. When they were identified, they reburied them from this place again, and they were -- the bodies -- the remains were returned back to the families. And, again, the families then, during the funeral, buried them -- at least three of them in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean, Mr. Janc, that there is no mass grave at Vragolovi, and are you able to tell the Trial Chamber if the OTP and you, as an investigator, are aware of the circumstances in which each of those individuals was killed, the ones that you referred to just now that had been returned to Visoko and buried there? Did they all die at the same time, in the same place, and in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is mass grave -- actually, there is a grave in Vragolovi which was exhumed in 2001 and where nine bodies were found. For all of them, we have autopsy records which says that the death of these bodies was violent. It means they were executed. We have those documents, and I think I refer to them in my report as well. If they died at the same time, that's difficult to determine, based on when they were exhumed. We know for some of them, we have some statements which says that two of those individuals, and I'm referring to Mehmed Hajric and Amir Imamovic, were taken out of Rogatica, Rasadnik prison, in the middle of August and never seen again. We know from other statements, testimonies and documents that Avdo Palic was taken out of Vanikov Mlin Prison at the beginning of September, 4th to 5th or 5th to 6th of September, 1995. It's difficult to say if they were killed at the same time or not. What we can see from the exhumation records is that bodies found there were next to each other, mostly, but body of Avdo Palic was over the body of someone else, so it's possible, theoretically, that other bodies were buried there first and later on Avdo Palic was placed over the other bodies and buried there as well. So I can't exclude that possibility. And we have a sketch of Eva Klonowski where you can see exactly how the bodies were distributed inside the grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, could you please repeat the name of this prison you mentioned in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is Rasadnik Prison in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please check the transcript, if it's written correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is almost correctly, just instead of O, it should be A, the second letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. You didn't answer my question. Was the case of death of all the persons found in the Vragolovi mass grave something that was the same for all the persons there? Did it occur in the same way, in the same time, and in which circumstances? Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we don't have any information about that, and I think there is no pathologist on this earth who could identify this issue, so who could say if they were killed at the same time or not. This is only possible if the actual death occurred during a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. You said just now that Torlak said this and this other person said that. Was it possible, in conversations with the prisoners who were in Rogatica, to find out who disappeared from the group of prisoners and why they didn't appear --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter kindly asks Mr. Tolimir to repeat the last word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the last word. The interpretation stopped with --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last word was "exchange," "exchange," why they didn't appear at the exchange at the same time as the others who were with them in the Rasadnik Prison.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are several statements. Not only of Mr. Torlak, also other individuals who were imprisoned in Rasadnik Prison and later on exchanged were testifying or talking about these individuals and then -- and when they disappeared from a prison and then never appeared back again. And some of them also testified or stated that they were maltreated and beaten badly, and they concluded that they were killed. Nobody actually has seen that, when and how they were killed, but they never appeared back again and they were never exchanged. And now we know where they were found. And from the exhumation records, we can see that they were killed, executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And in these witness statements, were they all taken out of the prison at the same time, the same day, and were they all killed at the same time or, according to these witness statements, were these persons taken out at different times and killed at different times?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From these witness statements, we can't conclude anything with a certain level of certainty, because even the dates when they were taken out are different from these statements. Some of them think that they were taken out at the beginning of August, some of them in the middle of August, some of them soon after they arrived, so we can't conclude exactly when they were taken out. Most of them are talking that they were taken out, and now I'm referring to Mehmed Hajric and Amir Imamovic, at around the same time, even the same day, and they never appeared again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And does the OTP have documents on the basis of which one can reach any kind of degree of reliability as to when they were taken, by whom, in what way? It doesn't have to be a high degree of reliability.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are witness statements. And I think one of the witnesses who will be talking about them is coming soon to testify here in front of this Trial Chamber, so he'll be able to explain these details more precisely than I can do because he was an eye-witness of this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But I wanted to ask about any documents in the OTP about that. Did you see documents of that kind? Can they be used, can they be looked at?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are now referring to any kind of documents produced by the VRS at the time or any kind of documents produced by the wardens or the personnel who was in charge of this prison, no, we don't have any such documents. Everything we have are witness statements of the prisoners who were kept in this prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Can you please tell us if you spoke with each of the prisoners who was in prison in order to gather information about persons found in the so-called mass grave at Vragolovi? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we haven't talked to every single one of them. We have talked to some of them. But we have statements which were provided to the OTP by the BiH authorities from other prisoners who were there and were interviewed after they were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you look into those statements, and did you see, on the basis of that, whether they were executed at the same time, at different times, and were the perpetrators of the executions the same persons in all the cases? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was reviewing these statements, and what I already said just a few minutes ago, their statements are not consistent. You know, they are different in the matter of when this might happen. But they are consistent in a way that they say that they disappear at one point in time on one day and that they never appear back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. And can you please tell us, if there isn't a high degree of reliability, is the assessment of the investigator important in that case, or should one be guided by findings of expert witnesses or experts who establish the time of death, the manner of death, and the circumstances that it occurred? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the manner and the cause of death was established, and I testified that you can find from autopsy records that their death was violent, that they were executed; that is what was established. The exact time of death, I think it will be very difficult to establish, but we can say it might be around the time when they disappeared from the prison in 1995. And what also can be established from this perspective is that they were under control of the VRS, and then they were last seen when they were in their hands, and later on they were found in Vragolovi grave, which is about four kilometres away only from Rasadnik Prison, so very close to where they were last seen. And this is territory of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, it is 7.00. We have to adjourn. I think you are not able to finish the whole cross-examination. We should continue it next week. Can you give us an indication how much more time you need for the conclusion of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't have any more questions for this witness, other than to say thank you to him for the answers that he gave and to wish him success in his work. The only question I have is this: Did he make the report for the Court or did he make the report for the Prosecution? This is the only answer I would like from this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you help us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, and -- I can help you. I made this report for the benefit of this trial, for this Trial Chamber, so for this Court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Defence did not get it. We thank you. We didn't receive it as a report that was drafted for the Defence. We received it as a document drafted for the OTP. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it this concludes your cross-examination. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Vanderpuye, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Indeed, I do, Mr. President, and I won't be able to finish it in the time that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We don't have any time. So perhaps we can put it off to a more convenient date for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would only like to consider if it is helpful to continue with the re-examination just on Monday - I don't know how much time you would indicate - so that there is no interruption. That would be, for the Chamber, for a better understanding of the testimony of this witness, but even for the witness, I think, if we could conclude that on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. President. I think that's a good idea. We do have a witness who is arriving that must testify on Monday, but I think the re-direct examination won't be long and shouldn't interfere with his ability to testify to completion on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is, of course, in your hands, but you have heard my, yes, proposal how to deal with this witness further. We have to adjourn for the week. Mr. Janc, thank you very much. On Monday, we are sitting in the afternoon in this courtroom at 2.15. You are reminded again that it's not allowed to have contact on the content of your testimony with either party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of May, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
